sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File purpose and imports
sections.what: Describes the two shared controls and the server addresses they use, then loads the React state tools, icons and the shared request helper.
sections.why: The header is written so a reader knows which address each control calls.
sections.watch_out: The addresses in the header are documentation; if the server routes change, this comment must change too.

sections.name: saveAttachment, msg
sections.title: Saving a server file and reading error text
sections.what: Downloads a file from the server, takes the suggested name from the reply, and starts a browser save. It also turns any error into readable text, falling back to a generic message.
sections.why: Both download buttons need the same save step, so it is written once.
sections.watch_out: The file name is read with a pattern match on the header, so unusual header formats can fall back to the default name.

sections.name: CancelRunButton
sections.title: Stop-run button with confirmation
sections.what: Shows a Cancel run button only for queued or running runs. Pressing it asks for confirmation, then sends the stop request, handles the already-finished case with a clear note, and refreshes the page afterwards either way.
sections.why: The comment on the 409 case explains that a refresh shows the true final outcome.
sections.watch_out: The page is refreshed even after a failure, so the screen always shows the server's current state after pressing it.

sections.name: LedgerDownload
sections.title: Download the research ledger
sections.what: A button that downloads the full JSON record of every stage. It works for partial, failed and cancelled runs, as its tooltip says.
sections.why: The tooltip explains that the ledger is kept for runs that did not finish.
sections.watch_out: The button stays disabled while the download is busy, so a slow server looks frozen until it replies.

sections.name: WorkbookDownload
sections.title: Download the Excel workbook
sections.what: A button that downloads the research workbook with directory, cost, schedule, sources, verification, calculations and overrun-reason signals.
sections.why: The tooltip lists what the workbook contains, so the owner knows what to expect.
sections.watch_out: The workbook is only as complete as the server makes it, and this button does not check which sheets are included.

summary: Provides shared buttons for stopping a running scan and for downloading its research ledger (JSON) or workbook (Excel).
purpose: Lets a user stop a scan that is still queued or running, and lets them save the scan's records to their computer.
why: The file header says these controls are shared by Reality Scan and Lessons Learnt, so they live in one place rather than being copied into each tool.
how: 1. The cancel button shows only while a run is queued or running. 2. Pressing it opens a confirmation box. 3. Confirming sends a POST request to the run's cancel address. 4. A conflict reply (409) is shown as a note that the run already finished. 5. The download buttons send a GET request to the ledger or workbook address, read the file name from the response header, and trigger a browser download. 6. Any failure is shown as a short red message beside the button.
inputs: The base address of the API, the run id, the run status (for cancel), and a fallback file name used if the server sends none.
outputs: A cancel request to the server, saved files on the user's computer, and short error messages on screen.
risks: Stopping a run is final for the rest of the run: finished stages are kept, unfinished stages will not run, and no deck is produced. The confirmation box is the only safeguard.
debug: If cancel fails, check the response shown in the red message and the run's status. If a download has the wrong name, check the Content-Disposition response header. If a download does nothing, check that the server returns a file and not an error page.
